To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of SPSII in source leaves is higher compared to sink leaves and that the expression of ShST4 is higher in the sink than in the source leaf.
the expression of sucrose transport and sucrose-phosphate-synthase genes is different between the sink and source leaf, and between the rind and the pith, but not between the different cultivars.

the transcript levels of sucrose-phosphat-synthase II (SPSI) were higher in source leaves than in sink leaves, but the levels of sucrose transportes ShSUT4 and ShSUT1 were similar in source and sink leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of sucrose transport in sugarcane and the role of sucrose phosphate synthetase (SPS) and SUTs in sucrose transport in leaves and internode of sugarcane.
a better understanding of the sucrose metabolism in sugarcane and with the development of new tools for improving the yield potential of sugarcane.
the regulation of sucrose metabolism in leaves and internode of high-yielding sugarcane cultivar.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sucrose transporters are not the rate limiting factor in the sink and in the source leaves of high yielding cultivars.
sucrose transporters play a role in the internode, but not in the leaves, and that the role of SPSII is more complex than previously thought.
the expression of sucrose transport and SPSII is tissue-specific and cultivar-dependent, but the expression pattern is different between source and sink leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sucrose transporters SUT1A and 4 are expressed at higher levels in source than sink leaves, but that SUT4 is expressed at higher level in rind compared to the pith of internodes.
the expression levels of SPS, ShSUT4, and ShSUC2 in source leaves and in immature internodes were higher than in sink leaves and mature internodes.
the sucrose transporters are expressed in the internode rind and peth, but that the expression is lower in the pith than in the rind, except for one cultivar.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sucrose transporters in the internode rind may play a role in sucrose export to the phloem and the sucrose transport system in the internodes is more complex than in the leaves.

the transcript levels of sucrose transport and sucrose metabolism genes are different between the source and the sink leaves, between the rind and the pith of the mature internode, and between the cultivar.

the transcript levels of ShSUTs are not a good indication of the sucrose concentration in sugarcane tissues, which is the main reason that ShSUTs cannot be used as markers for high-yielding cultivar selection.
